research: https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/StopMotionLighting — 'stop-motion lighting': each lightning flash freezes a new moment, so the change happens in the dark between flashes; the audience then doubts what it saw. Our cut hides the price swap inside the white.

https://www.gaylydreadful.com/blog/feature-flashing-lights-overused-horror-clich-or-crucial-film-element — flash-reveal horror (camera-flash/demon example, The Ring remake frames hidden in flashes): one thing changes between flashes, everything else stays still, so the change is what you notice.
https://runware.ai/docs/models/google-nano-banana-2/guides/prompting — Nano Banana 2 renders text; put exact copy in quotes, keep it to a few words, and name the treatment (handwritten marker, card).

https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/ultimate-prompting-guide-for-nano-banana — Google: quote the exact text and describe its placement like a designer; photo/film vocabulary steers realism.
https://www.veed.io/learn/nano-banana-prompting-guide — film stock / camera terms push photorealism; grain has to be asked for explicitly.

https://www.veo3gen.app/blog/veo-31-imagetovideo-prompt-sandwich-a-3layer-template-to-animate-one-photo-witho — image-to-video: treat the still as the fixed reference and write only what changes; 'locked-off tripod shot, no zoom, no pan, no tilt' cuts drift; one action + at most one small environmental change.

https://hailuoai.video/knowledge/fix-ai-video-flicker-stable-lighting — vague lighting prompts make the model re-solve light every frame (flicker); keep the light in the still and describe only the timed event in the motion prompt.
https://www.renderforest.com/blog/image-to-video-ai-prompts — state explicitly what must stay fixed (text, layout) in the motion prompt.

https://invideo.io/faq/how-do-you-prompt-ai-video-tools-to-generate-electricity/ — generic 'add lightning' gives a static glow; describe how the light behaves moment to moment (blows out, hard shadows, snaps back).
notes: Three places not yet seen: (a) the till counter, insert, lightning through the front glass door behind it — the thematic hit, you meet it last at the till; (b) the chest freezer in the back corner, medium, lightning through a small grilled frosted window (grille shadows, double flash); (c) the front window display ledge, wide from inside, the whole street lit and the goods silhouetted. BEFORE and AFTER stills are word-for-word the same except the two price cards plus ONE deliberate horror jump-cut change, written as a separate final sentence so it can be deleted for a pure price-only swap: (a) till drawer hangs open and empty, (b) frost crawls onto the outside of the freezer glass, (c) the streetlamp outside is dead. Generate BEFORE first, then AFTER; if the AFTER re-frames, regenerate AFTER with the BEFORE still attached as reference. Cut point: last bright frame of the BEFORE clip's flash to the over-bright first frame of AFTER. Chocolate bar unbranded throughout. Every prompt ends 'Thanks.'

options.place: the till counter (the place you meet it last)
options.label: insert at the till, lightning through the front door
options.still_before: Close insert photograph at counter height in a small British corner shop at night: a scratched cream laminate shop counter at the till. On the counter, side by side, sit a loaf of plain white sliced bread in a clear plastic bag twisted shut, and a small chocolate bar in a plain purple foil wrapper with no logo and no writing. Behind them, an old beige cash register with its drawer shut, a dented coin tray and a curling roll of till receipt. Behind the counter, out of focus, the shop's glass front door shows black wet street and one orange streetlamp. Leaning on the loaf is a small white card price ticket handwritten in thick black marker that reads exactly "£5". Leaning on the chocolate bar is a smaller white card handwritten in thick black marker that reads exactly "10p". Candid snapshot on cheap 400-speed colour negative film at night, pushed: heavy visible grain, slightly soft focus, muddy blacks, sickly teal-green cast from old fluorescent tubes, faint warm sodium orange from the street. Vertical 9:16. Nobody in the shop, no people, no hands, no shadows of people. No brand names or logos anywhere; every packet in the background is blurred and unreadable. Thanks.
